one_liner: LLNL user-space mmap replacement built on userfaultfd; beats Linux mmap for large-page, out-of-core reads with tuned paging.
what_it_does: UMap maps a file (or a custom Umap::Store backend such as the multi-file SparseStore or a network store) into memory and services its page faults in user space through userfaultfd, keeping an application-sized buffer of cached pages. The C API mirrors mmap: umap(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, off) and uunmap(), plus umap_ex() in C++ for a custom Store, umap_prefetch(), umap_fetch_and_pin() and umap_flush(). Only UMAP_PRIVATE mappings are supported.
how_it_is_fast: Faults are delivered as userfaultfd messages and resolved by pools of filler and evictor threads, with decoupled fault queues, configurable read-ahead and load balancing across workers. The UMap page size is independent of the 4 KiB system page (UMAP_PAGESIZE), so one fault can pull megabytes in a single bulk read; fewer faults and larger transfers are where the gain over kernel mmap comes from. Eviction uses high/low watermarks on a bounded buffer instead of the global page cache.
when_to_use: Out-of-core, read-mostly scans or graph analytics (Ligra BFS-style) over files much larger than RAM on NVMe or Optane, where coarse paging pays off
Workloads that tolerate large UMap pages (64 KiB and up; the paper snippet reports the best result at 8 MiB pages)
HPC codes that want per-application control of page size, read-ahead, buffer size and worker counts without kernel changes
Datasets split over many files or a remote store, via SparseStore or a custom Umap::Store
when_not_to_use: Small-page random access: per the paper snippet UMap only overtakes mmap when the page size exceeds 64 KiB
Shared mappings or multi-process sharing: UMAP_SHARED is not supported
Containers with Docker's default seccomp profile, or hosts where vm.unprivileged_userfaultfd=0 and you are not root

Write-heavy or correctness-critical data without testing: open issue #71 reports pages changing without being marked dirty (eviction miscompare under umapsort, 128 threads); write mode needs kernel >= 5.7 and 5.7-5.9 can hang on writes
Programs creating many mappings: open issue #91 reports ENOMEM from UFFDIO_REGISTER past about 900 regions; LGPL-2.1 may also rule it out for static linking

integration.dependencies: Linux kernel headers with userfaultfd; no other libraries
integration.platforms: Linux only; kernel >= 4.3 read-only, >= 5.7 read/write (>= 5.10 preferred); any architecture with userfaultfd
integration.thread_safety: Not documented per call; the runtime itself is multi-threaded (filler and evictor pools, default hardware_concurrency each) and guards region setup with a global mutex
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — mmap-shaped signature, but separate umap/uunmap calls, private mappings only, and different fault/flush semantics

gotchas: Default CMake build type is Debug and ENABLE_LOGGING defaults to On; build with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release before measuring

Write-protect (read/write) mode is chosen at compile time from the build host's kernel headers; a binary built against 5.10 headers fails at runtime on an older kernel, and some distros (Ubuntu 20.04.2) ship headers that hide the feature
UMAP_BUFSIZE defaults to 90% of free memory and filler/evictor counts default to hardware_concurrency each, so an untuned process can grab most of RAM and many threads
Tuning is by environment variables (UMAP_PAGESIZE, UMAP_BUFSIZE, UMAP_PAGE_FILLERS, UMAP_PAGE_EVICTORS, watermarks), read at runtime start, not per region by default
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick UMap when you need an unmodified kernel and a library-only, mmap-shaped API with tunable large pages; FastMap and vmcache/exmap claim larger gains over mmap but need a kernel module or custom kernel, and TriCache targets transparent caching of whole applications rather than explicit mappings.
verified_claims_summary: All numbers are first-party and come from paper snippets (PDFs on osti.gov, arxiv.org and web.cels.anl.gov are blocked here): 1.22-1.9x over an optimized kernel-based service across intra-node concurrency, 1.2-1.5x over system mmap on Ligra applications, and about 2.5x over mmap at 8 MiB UMap pages on NVMe/Optane, with UMap ahead only above 64 KiB pages. Hardware, kernel and compiler were not visible in the snippets, and the repo has no benchmark code (applications are in LLNL/umap-apps).
status_note: Recent commits on develop (last 2026-07-21) but the issue tracker is quiet, with 2018-2022 bugs (#71 data miscompares, #91 ENOMEM) still open; LGPL-2.1, small enough to build from source on Linux.
sources_read: WebSearch snippets: osti.gov purl 1829975 (TPDS 2021), osti.gov purl 1574628 and arxiv 1910.07566 (MCHPC 2019)
